post.description: The key keeps its id, prefix, name, scopes and expiry, so only the secret changes on the device. The replaced secret keeps working for gracePeriodMin minutes (default 1440 = 24 h, 0 = stops at once; previousKeyExpiresAt in the answer); rotating again during a grace period ends the older secret at once. Other services cache an active key for up to 60 s, so the replaced secret may still pass there for that long after its grace period. A key with a scope the caller could not grant (ais:ingest for org_admins) cannot be rotated by them.

get.description: The records of GET /audit-logs with the same filters, scope and default range (newest first) as one streamed RFC 4180 file (`Content-Disposition: attachment`): the header line `id,at,source,actorType,actorId,actorName,actorEmail,orgId,orgName,action,targetType,targetId,targetLabel,ip,userAgent,meta`, CRLF line ends, the values of the JSON records (empty for null, meta as JSON). Text cells that start with =, +, -, @, tab or CR get a leading apostrophe, so spreadsheet programs never run them as formulas (OWASP CSV injection). Errors before the first byte are problem details; a failure during the transfer aborts the connection, so a cut file never looks complete.
